note: By train where possible: Metro-North, the LIRR and Amtrak reach most of these without a car, and each says how. Each says what to do there, in order, and when it is worth going; the ones marked overnight are weekends, not days. Researched, not yet done.

items.title: Beacon and Dia Beacon
items.transit: Metro-North Hudson Line from Grand Central, about 1h30
items.why: The best day out by train from New York. Dia Beacon is a former Nabisco box-printing factory on the river, filled with enormous minimalist art under sawtooth skylights: Richard Serra's steel spirals you walk inside, Louise Bourgeois's spiders. It opens Friday to Monday. Then walk up Main Street, and climb Mount Beacon if you have the legs.
items.hoursNote: A place to spend the day, not a door — what is in it keeps its own hours

stops.text: Metro-North from Grand Central; sit on the left for the river
Dia Beacon, two minutes from the station — Serra, Bourgeois, Warhol · Friday to Monday, 10 to 5
Lunch on Main Street, a mile up the hill
Mount Beacon at the east end of town: a steep hour up to the fire tower
A beer by the river at the station before the train home

items.season: All year; October for the foliage from the train and the mountain. Dia is closed Tuesday to Thursday.

items.title: Storm King Art Center
items.transit: About 1h15 by car up the Palisades Parkway; weekend coach packages from Port Authority
items.why: Five hundred acres of fields and hills in the Hudson Valley with giant sculptures set into the landscape: Andy Goldsworthy's stone wall snaking through the trees and into a pond, Maya Lin's rippling earth waves, Serra's steel plates across a meadow. You walk or cycle between them. Buy tickets ahead; autumn weekends sell out.
items.hoursNote: A place to spend the day, not a door — what is in it keeps its own hours

stops.text: Book a timed ticket — they are needed for entry and parking
Hire a bike at the entrance to cover the whole park
Goldsworthy's Storm King Wall, in the woods to the west
Maya Lin's Storm King Wavefield, at the north end
Picnic on the hill by the museum building, with the Catskills behind

items.season: April to mid-December, closed Tuesdays. Autumn is the best and busiest; peak weekend prices run from late September to 8 November.

items.title: Cold Spring and the Hudson Highlands
items.why: A nineteenth-century river village where the train drops you at the foot of Main Street: antique shops, a bandstand on the water, and Storm King Mountain directly across the Hudson. Breakneck Ridge and its station are closed for construction until 2027, so hike Bull Hill from the edge of the village instead, for the same view with fewer people.
items.hoursNote: A place to spend the day, not a door — what is in it keeps its own hours

stops.text: Metro-North to Cold Spring
The bandstand and dock at the bottom of Main Street, looking at Storm King
Bull Hill (Mount Taurus) from the Washburn trailhead: a steep 3 to 4 hours round
Or Boscobel, a Federal-style house with the best lawn view on the river
Dinner on Main Street before the train back

items.season: October is peak foliage and very busy; go on a weekday if you can. Breakneck Ridge is closed until mid-2027.

items.title: Sleepy Hollow and the river towns
items.transit: Metro-North to Tarrytown or Philipse Manor, about 50 min
items.why: Washington Irving's village, and in October the most atmospheric place near New York: the Old Dutch Church and its hillside burial ground, where Irving is buried, the bridge from The Legend of Sleepy Hollow, and the old river towns up the Hudson. Stay for dark, when the Jack O'Lantern Blaze lights up a manor at Croton, ten minutes north.
items.hoursNote: A place to spend the day, not a door — what is in it keeps its own hours

stops.text: Metro-North to Philipse Manor, the station on the Sleepy Hollow side
The Old Dutch Church and Sleepy Hollow Cemetery — Irving's grave, and the Rockefellers'
The Headless Horseman Bridge on the Pocantico River
Kykuit, the Rockefeller estate, by tour from the visitor centre
After dark: the Great Jack O'Lantern Blaze at Croton — book it

items.season: October is the whole point: the Blaze, the Horseman, the leaves. Kykuit tours run spring to autumn.
items.imageSubject: Old Dutch Church of Sleepy Hollow

items.title: Philadelphia
items.priceNote: Train from ~$30 each way; most history is free
items.transit: Amtrak from Moynihan, about 1h20; NJ Transit and SEPTA cost less and take longer
items.why: The city where the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution were signed, an hour and a half away and cheaper than New York in every way. See Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell, eat through Reading Terminal Market, and spend the afternoon at the Barnes, a private collection of Renoirs, Cézannes and Matisses hung exactly as its founder left them.
items.hoursNote: A place to spend the day, not a door — what is in it keeps its own hours

stops.text: Amtrak to 30th Street Station
Independence Hall (free timed ticket) and the Liberty Bell across the street
Reading Terminal Market for lunch: a roast pork sandwich at DiNic's
The Barnes Foundation on the Parkway — book
A cheesesteak in South Philly before the train, and argue about which one

items.season: All year. Spring and autumn are best for walking.

items.title: Hudson and Olana
items.priceNote: Train ~$35 each way; Olana grounds free
items.transit: Amtrak from Moynihan to Hudson, about 2 hours along the river
items.why: The train ride up the east bank of the Hudson is among the most beautiful in America, and at the end of it is Hudson: a whaling town turned into a mile of antique shops, galleries and restaurants on Warren Street. Across the river on a hilltop is Olana, the Persian-style house the painter Frederic Church built to look at the view he painted.
items.hoursNote: A place to spend the day, not a door — what is in it keeps its own hours

stops.text: Amtrak up the river; sit on the left
Walk Warren Street from the river end to the top
Lunch on Warren Street
Olana, ten minutes by taxi: the house by tour, the grounds free
The Hudson River Skywalk over the bridge to Thomas Cole's house, if there is time

items.season: May to October for the grounds; October for the colour. Olana's house tours need booking.

items.title: New Haven
items.transit: Metro-North New Haven Line from Grand Central, about 2 hours
items.why: The best pizza in America, argued with a straight face, and two of the best free museums on the East Coast. Queue at Frank Pepe's or Sally's on Wooster Street for coal-fired apizza, the white clam pie at Pepe's. Before it, walk Yale's gothic courtyards and see the Yale University Art Gallery and the Center for British Art, both free.
items.hoursNote: A place to spend the day, not a door — what is in it keeps its own hours

stops.text: Metro-North to New Haven Union Station
Yale University Art Gallery, free: Van Gogh's Night Café
The Yale Center for British Art across the street, free, in a Louis Kahn building
Walk the Old Campus and the courtyards
Wooster Street: the white clam pie at Frank Pepe's, or Sally's across the road

items.season: All year; weekday lunch is the way round the pizza queues.

items.title: Montauk and the end of Long Island
items.priceNote: A weekend: lodging is the cost
items.transit: The LIRR or the Hampton Jitney, about 3 hours — a weekend
items.why: The far eastern tip of Long Island, a fishing town with surf beaches rather than the Hamptons' hedges. In summer it is a party; in September and October it is quiet, the water is still warm and the rooms are cheaper. Stand under the lighthouse that George Washington commissioned, surf Ditch Plains, and eat lobster rolls on the dock.
items.hoursNote: A place to spend the day, not a door — what is in it keeps its own hours

stops.text: LIRR to Montauk, or the Jitney from Midtown
Montauk Point Lighthouse, commissioned by Washington, finished 1796
Ditch Plains for surfing or watching it
Lobster roll by the harbour
Sunset from the bluffs at Camp Hero

items.season: September and October are the best: warm water, no crowds. Summer weekends are packed and expensive.

items.title: The North Fork
items.transit: About 2 hours by car; the LIRR runs to Greenport on a limited timetable
items.why: The quieter fork of Long Island: potato fields turned vineyards, farm stands, and Greenport, an old whaling harbour at the end of the road. Taste at two or three wineries along Route 25, buy apple cider doughnuts and pumpkins at the farm stands, and eat oysters in Greenport. Somebody drives; or take the train and hire bikes.
items.hoursNote: A place to spend the day, not a door — what is in it keeps its own hours

stops.text: Two tastings along Main Road (Route 25)
A farm stand for cider doughnuts and whatever is being picked
Greenport harbour and the 1920 carousel
Oysters in Greenport
Or the ferry to Shelter Island and back

items.season: September and October: harvest, pumpkins and the best light. Summer weekends mean traffic on the LIE.

items.title: The Catskills: Kaaterskill Falls and Phoenicia
items.priceNote: Free trails; lodging is the cost
items.transit: About 2h30 by car up the Thruway — a weekend
items.why: The mountains the Hudson River School painted, two and a half hours north. Kaaterskill Falls drops 260 feet in two steps and is one of the highest in the state; the view from the platform is the painting. Stay in Phoenicia or Woodstock, eat well, and spend the second day on the fire towers and the creeks.
items.hoursNote: A place to spend the day, not a door — what is in it keeps its own hours

stops.text: Kaaterskill Falls from the viewing platform on Laurel House Road — stay on the marked trail
North–South Lake for the Escarpment Trail and the view from Artist's Rock
Woodstock for the evening
Breakfast in Phoenicia next morning
A fire-tower hike — Overlook Mountain above Woodstock

items.season: Foliage peaks in the first half of October. The falls are icy and dangerous in winter.

items.title: New Paltz, Mohonk and Minnewaska
items.priceNote: Mohonk Preserve day pass; state park parking
items.transit: About 1h45 by car; Trailways buses run to New Paltz
items.why: The Shawangunk Ridge, the Gunks: white cliffs that are the East Coast's great climbing crag, and on top a chain of sky lakes. Minnewaska's lake sits in white rock with carriage roads round it that anyone can walk or cycle. Mohonk Preserve has the cliffs, the climbers, and the Victorian tower at Sky Top.
items.hoursNote: A place to spend the day, not a door — what is in it keeps its own hours

stops.text: The Trapps at Mohonk Preserve: watch the climbers on the carriage road under the cliffs
Minnewaska State Park: the lake loop, and Awosting Falls
An orchard on Route 299 in apple season
New Paltz for dinner, on Main Street

items.season: May to October; mid-October for the colour. Minnewaska's lots fill early on autumn weekends.

items.title: Rockaway Beach
items.transit: The A train, or the NYC Ferry from Wall Street, about an hour
items.why: New York City's surf beach, at the end of the A train: miles of sand and a rebuilt concrete boardwalk, with surf lessons at the designated surfing beaches and taco stands on the boardwalk in summer. It is a subway ride from Manhattan and feels like another town. The ferry from Wall Street is the scenic way.
items.hoursNote: A place to spend the day, not a door — what is in it keeps its own hours

stops.text: NYC Ferry from Wall Street, or the A train
The surfing beaches around Beach 90th Street
Tacos on the boardwalk
Sunset from Fort Tilden, the wilder beach to the west

items.season: Summer for swimming; September and early October are warm and nearly empty. Lifeguards only in season.
